purpose: Broad candidate lexicon for turn-taking and uncertainty detection in Hindi, English, Hinglish and selected regional-influenced worker speech.
important_limit: No finite list covers every dialect, spelling, accent or site-specific phrase. This file intentionally distinguishes seed phrases from generated candidates. Validate with consented recordings and avoid treating any phrase as a filler without context.
usage_rules: Use the phrase as a cue, not a deterministic command; context and prosody matter.
Do not end a turn on 'haan', 'achha', 'right', 'hmm' or a pause alone if the utterance appears unfinished.
Do not assume 'bas' always means done; it may mean 'just/only'.
Do not treat 'nahi' as rejection of the report unless it answers a confirmation question.
Do not treat 'theek hai' as report approval unless the current bot question asks for confirmation.
When a worker says they are unsure about a critical number, ID, location or hazard, ask a targeted follow-up.
Regional examples are illustrative, not exhaustive and may be unnatural for some speakers; ask local speakers to review.
Generated candidates are coverage prompts for annotation, not evidence that every phrase is commonly used.
